To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1a) Bayesian neural networks are able to construct accurate response models for direct mail purchase incidence modelling; that (1b) a combined use all three RFM categories is advocated by Bayesian neural network learning; that (2) the inclusion of customer and company interaction variables, as well as the use of credit facilities, significantly improves the predictive power of RFM response models.
the use of neural networks for response modelling is feasible and that the use of RFM variables is recommended, but that the use of non-RFM variables is even more so.

the Bayesian neural networks outperform the traditional statistical response models and that the inclusion of non-RFM predictors in the RFM framework significantly enhances the predictive power of these RFM classifiers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a repeat purchase model for a direct mail company, using Bayesian neural network learning.
the use of Bayesian neural network techniques for purchase incidence modelling in a direct marketing context.
the application of neural network learning to a real world problem, and with the use of Bayesian neural networks for this task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusion of customer profiling variables, in addition to the traditionally discussed Receny, Frequency and Monetary variables, leads to significantly improved purchase incidence modelling.
a combined use of RFM and non RFM customer profiling predictors offers the best predictive power.
a combined RFM classifier with a set of non RFM interaction variables is the most powerful predictor of purchase incidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Bayesian neural network learning offers a viable alternative for RFM based response modelling, that the ARD method can be used to guide variable selection and that the inclusion of non-RFM variables allows to improve the predictive power of response models based on the RFM framework.
Bayesian neural networks offer an attractive alternative for purchase incidence modeling in direct marketing, especially if the models are enriched by the inclusion non RFM variables.

the use of Bayesian neural networks for repeat purchase modelling is promising, and that a combined use of RFM and other customer profiling variables is a fruitful approach to increase the predictive power of response models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian framework is an attractive alternative for the implementation of neural networks, especially for the purpose of direct marketing.
the Bayesian neural network approach is a promising tool for purchase incidence modelling.
Bayesian neural networks are a viable alternative for the construction of response models in the context of direct mail.
